gaps.quote: a procedure that is to run in near-linear time
gaps.note: The page uses near-linear time as the target for procedures without defining it or linking to a page that does.

gaps.quote: The tape lemmas rely on splitting an array on a digit
gaps.note: The tape lemmas are named but never explained or linked, so the reader cannot tell which results are meant.

gaps.quote: splitting an array on a digit
gaps.note: The reader does not know what a digit of an array is or how an array is split on one; the page neither explains nor links it.
Aligned streams are not defined on this page and no link is given.

gaps.quote: merging them back in linear time
gaps.note: The claim that merging the aligned streams takes linear time is asserted without a justification or a reference the reader could check.

gaps.quote: Each procedure is a fixed network whose wires each carry one stream
gaps.note: Network procedures, fixed networks and wires are not explained or linked, so the reader cannot follow how a procedure is a network.

gaps.term: same scan for every role stream
gaps.quote: so every role stream can be processed by the same scan
gaps.note: The page does not show why a single scan fits every role stream; nothing it states about the network's wires or role streams gives that conclusion.

gaps.quote: Fixed tracks are a further kind of stream storage in the paper
gaps.note: Fixed tracks are introduced as a kind of storage without explanation or a link.

gaps.term: running time unchanged by fixed tracks
gaps.quote: Using them therefore does not change the order of the running time.
gaps.note: The page states that fixed tracks leave the order of running time unchanged but gives no reason, and the word therefore has no visible premise.
